Reading the Authorization Header

How a token issued by /auth/login gets back to the server on every later request.

Login (previous topic) hands a client a token, but doesn't do anything with it beyond that — a client has to send it back on every request that needs to be authenticated, and this project follows the standard convention for where: an Authorization header, shaped Bearer <token>. middleware/ authenticate.js is what reads it:

// Figure 4.7: turning a header into req.user (src/middleware/authenticate.js)
export default (req, res, next) => {
  const header = req.get('Authorization');
  const token = header?.startsWith('Bearer ') ? header.slice('Bearer '.length) : null;

  if (!token) {
    return next(new ApiError(401, 'Authentication required'));
  }

  try {
    const payload = verifyToken(token);
    req.user = { id: payload.sub, role: payload.role };
    next();
  } catch {
    next(new ApiError(401, 'Invalid or expired token'));
  }
};

req.get('Authorization') reads the header; ?.startsWith('Bearer ') guards against it being missing entirely (header would be undefined, and undefined?.startsWith short-circuits to undefined rather than throwing) as well as present but wrongly shaped. No token at all is a 401 before verifyToken is even called — there's nothing to check.

verifyToken (previous topic) is the one call doing the real work, wrapped in a try/catch because it throws — on a tampered signature, a token signed with a different secret, or one that's simply expired — rather than returning a pass/fail result the way safeParse does (Lesson 3's validate.js). Catching that throw and forwarding a clean 401 ApiError either way (missing token, or one that fails to verify) means a controller downstream never sees the difference — only that authentication failed.

On success, req.user = { id: payload.sub, role: payload.role } is the entire payoff: from this point in the middleware chain onward, any route this runs in front of can read req.user and trust it, without ever touching a token, a header, or verifyToken itself again.
